How a Texas web designer in Big Sandy covers a state this size

Texas is too big for anyone to be local everywhere, and a web designer who claims an office in every metro is usually renting a mailbox. Dominion Web Design Pro is one Texas web designer, Maurice Johnson, working out of Big Sandy in Upshur County. He writes and builds every page himself and delivers the finished site by link, phone and email.

That setup decides how the service area works. East Texas is close enough to drive. The big Texas metros, where business owners search hardest for web design, each get a city page researched for that market. Metro Atlanta has its own set of researched pages. And a business anywhere else in the country can still order a site, because nothing about building one requires being in the same room.

Texas has roughly 3.5 million small businesses, second only to California, according to the U.S. Small Business Administration's Office of Advocacy. Many of them are owner-run shops, crews and offices that depend on nearby customers finding them. That is the business this site is built for.

Four circles of coverage

Each circle gets the same packages and the same hand-written standard. What changes is how well the city pages on this site already know your market.

1. Home turf: East Texas

Big Sandy, Gilmer, Tyler, Longview, Kilgore, Marshall and Gladewater. These are the towns Maurice knows from living here: the highways people drive to shop, the festivals that fill a square, the county offices that handle a DBA. If meeting in person would genuinely help, call and ask.

2. Texas metros with real search demand

In our keyword data, Houston, Dallas and Austin are the Texas cities with the most searches for "web design" plus the city name. Kingwood, Waco and El Paso also clear ten searches a month in our keyword data, so each one has its own researched page too, along with the Dallas and Austin suburbs covered earlier.

3. Georgia

Metro Atlanta has six hand-written pages: Atlanta, Lawrenceville, Decatur, McDonough, Conyers and Douglasville. The four newest were added because each town clears ten searches a month for web design in our keyword data.

4. The rest of the country

No city page does not mean no service. A plumber in Missouri or a salon in Arizona gets the same demo, the same packages and the same person on the other end of the email. The research simply happens for your towns when the project starts.

Why a website company in Texas should write for your town, not for "Texas"

Searches like "web design tx" and "website design company texas" are typed by people at the start of the hunt. By the time a homeowner in Katy or a restaurant manager in Waco is looking for a business, they search for the service and the town. A site that only says "serving all of Texas" gives Google nothing to match against that second search.

So the pages a Texas business needs are specific: a page for each service, and a page for each town that brings in work, each one saying something true about that place. That is the same method used on this site. It is also why page count is never the selling point here. We do not sell page counts; a few dozen pages that each earn their place beat a pile of copies with the city name swapped.

What changes from region to region is the detail. A Houston page has to deal with a city where more than a quarter of residents were born outside the country. An El Paso page has to deal with a border economy and a city that runs on Mountain Time. An East Texas page has to deal with rural customers who search before they drive twenty miles. The research behind each city page is about those differences.

What working with a remote Texas web designer looks like

  1. You ask for the demoOn the demo page or by phone. You give the business name, the trade and the towns you serve.
  2. You review it on your own phoneA link arrives with a preview site for your business. No meeting, no deposit.
  3. You pick a package, or you do notStarter, Pro or Agency, each a one-time price. Saying no costs nothing.
  4. Maurice researches and writesYour towns get researched the same way the city pages on this site were, then every page is written by hand and launched on your domain.

Which package fits a service area

The size of your service area is the best guide to the package. A shop that serves one town usually needs the Starter site, which already includes a service area page. A contractor working a county or two gets more from Pro, which adds 10 city pages, each researched and written from scratch. A company covering a whole region with several services is who the Agency package was built for: keyword research first, then a page for each town-and-service pair worth having.

Common questions

Is there a Texas web designer who will build my site before I pay?

Yes. Dominion Web Design Pro is run by Maurice Johnson in Big Sandy, Texas, and every project starts with a free demo built for your business name and trade. You look at it on your phone, and only then decide whether to buy Starter ($497), Pro ($997) or Agency ($1,997), all one-time prices.

Do you work with businesses outside Texas?

Yes. The work is delivered remotely, so a business in Ohio or Oregon gets the same process as one in Tyler: a demo by link, phone calls, and pages approved by email. The site has city pages for Texas and metro Atlanta because those are the places researched so far, not because other places are turned away.

Do you have an office in Houston, Dallas or Austin?

No. The only base is Big Sandy in East Texas. The city pages on this site explain each market honestly, and each one says plainly that there is no office there. If having a designer down the street matters a lot to you, that is a fair reason to hire someone local, and we would rather you know it up front.

What does a web design company in Texas usually charge?

Prices across Texas run from a few hundred dollars for a builder template to many thousands for an agency build, and many firms add monthly fees on top. Ours are fixed and public: $497, $997 or $1,997 one time, plus $49 a month for hosting and maintenance if you do not keep the AI agent. The small business website cost guide walks through what drives the range.

Can you write pages for every town my business serves?

That is what the Pro and Agency packages are for. Pro includes 10 city pages, each town researched and written from scratch. Agency starts with keyword research across your whole service area and adds a hand-written page for every town-and-service combination the research says is worth having, usually 30 to 60 pages. Here is how city pages work.
